subject: Income-tax Law
question_html: Which of the following best describes a 'return of income' under the Income-tax Act, 2025?

options.A: A prescribed statement through which an assessee furnishes particulars relating to his/its total income, tax liability, taxes paid, and other prescribed information for a tax year
options.B: A demand notice issued by the Assessing Officer specifying the amount of tax payable by the assessee for a tax year
options.C: A certificate issued by a chartered accountant confirming that the assessee's books of account have been audited
options.D: An acknowledgement issued by a bank confirming that advance tax has been deposited by the assessee

answer_html:

A return of income is a prescribed statement through which an assessee furnishes particulars of total income, tax liability, taxes paid, and other prescribed information for a tax year - it is the assessee's own declaration of income and resultant tax in the prescribed format.

question_html: The compulsory filing requirement based on holding a foreign asset, having signing authority in a foreign account, or being a beneficiary of a foreign asset, applies to which category of resident individual?

options.A: A resident who is 'other than not ordinarily resident' - i.e., a resident and ordinarily resident (ROR) individual; it does NOT apply to a resident but not ordinarily resident (RNOR) individual
options.B: It applies equally to both ROR and RNOR individuals, with no distinction drawn between the two categories for this specific compulsory-filing test

question_html: For the purposes of section 263(1), who is a 'beneficial owner' of an asset?

options.A: An individual who merely holds legal title to the asset in his own name, regardless of who actually provided the consideration for its acquisition
options.B: An individual who has provided, directly or indirectly, consideration for the asset for the immediate or future benefit, direct or indirect, of himself or any other person

Correct answer: (B) An individual who has provided, directly or indirectly, consideration for the asset for the immediate or future benefit, direct or indirect, of himself or any other person

'Beneficial owner', for the purpose of section 263, means an individual who has provided, directly or indirectly, consideration for the asset for the immediate or future benefit, direct or indirect, of himself or any other person - this is distinct from a mere 'beneficiary', who derives benefit but did not himself provide the consideration.

question_html: For the purposes of section 263(1), who is a 'beneficiary' of an asset?

options.A: An individual who has himself provided the consideration for the asset for the immediate or future benefit of himself or any other person
options.B: An individual who has been formally nominated in a will to inherit the asset upon the death of its current legal owner
options.C: An individual who derives benefit from the asset during the tax year, where the consideration for such asset has been provided by any person other than such beneficiary

A 'beneficiary', for the purpose of section 263, means an individual who derives benefit from the asset during the tax year, where the consideration for such asset has been provided by a person OTHER than the beneficiary himself - distinguishing a beneficiary from a 'beneficial owner', who himself provides the consideration.

Is the beneficiary independently required to compulsorily file a return under section 263(1) on account of this foreign asset?

options.A: Yes; every beneficiary of a foreign asset is compulsorily required to file a return under section 263(1), regardless of whether the income from that asset is separately taxed in the beneficial owner's hands
options.B: Yes, but only if the beneficiary is a non-resident, since resident beneficiaries are exempted from this requirement under all circumstances

Section 263(1) carves out an exception for a beneficiary: the compulsory-filing obligation on account of being a beneficiary of a foreign asset does not apply where the income arising from that asset is includible in the income of the beneficial owner - avoiding a duplicate compulsory-filing trigger for the same underlying asset/income.

question_html: A person other than a company or a firm (being an individual, HUF, AOP/BOI, or artificial juridical person) is required to furnish a return of income for a tax year if:

options.A: His total income (or the total income of any other person in respect of which he is assessable), computed WITHOUT giving effect to the deductions under sections 82 to 86 or under Chapter VIII, exceeds the basic exemption limit
options.B: His total income, computed AFTER giving full effect to all deductions under sections 82 to 86 and Chapter VIII, exceeds the basic exemption limit
options.C: His gross receipts from any business or profession, regardless of the resultant total income after all deductions and exemptions, exceed the basic exemption limit
options.D: His total income, before giving effect to any deduction, is less than the basic exemption limit, since only such persons are required to file a return to claim a refund

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) His total income (or the total income of any other person in respect of which he is assessable), computed WITHOUT giving effect to the deductions under sections 82 to 86 or under Chapter VIII, exceeds the basic exemption limit

The threshold test compares total income, computed WITHOUT giving effect to the deductions under sections 82 to 86 (relating to certain capital gains) or under Chapter VIII, against the basic exemption limit. This is a deliberately higher pre-deduction figure, ensuring that persons who reduce their income below the threshold only through deductions still remain within the filing requirement.

question_html: A return, once revised under section 263(5), is later discovered by the assessee to contain a further omission. Can the assessee revise the (already-revised) return a second time?

options.A: Yes; a revised return replaces the original return, and if a further omission or wrong statement is discovered in that revised return, a second revised return may be furnished within the same prescribed time limit (twelve months from the end of the relevant tax year, or before completion of assessment, whichever is earlier) - a return can be revised more than once within the prescribed time
options.B: No; a return can be revised only once under section 263(5), and any further omission discovered after the first revision can never be corrected through a second revised return
options.C: No; a second revision requires the assessee to first withdraw the first revised return through a separate formal application to the Assessing Officer, this being a mandatory precondition

answer_html:

Since a revised return replaces the original return, any further omission discovered in that revised return can be corrected by furnishing a second (or subsequent) revised return, so long as it is furnished within the same overall prescribed time limit under section 263(5) - the statute does not cap the number of permissible revisions within that window.

options.A: Where the updated return has the effect of INCREASING the total tax liability determined on the basis of the earlier return, this being specifically and expressly barred under section 263(6)

subject: Income-tax Law
question_html: Mr. A has already furnished an updated return under section 263(6) for tax year 2026-27. He later discovers yet another omission for the same tax year. Can he furnish a second updated return for tax year 2026-27?

options.A: No; an updated return cannot be updated again - once an updated return has already been furnished for a tax year, the updated-return provisions cease to apply for that tax year
options.B: Yes; there is no limit on the number of times an updated return can be furnished for the same tax year, so long as each successive filing is within the 48-month window
options.C: Yes, but only within 48 months from the end of the financial year succeeding the relevant tax year, this being the sole limiting condition on filing a second updated return
options.D: Yes, if the second updated return has the effect of reducing Mr. A's tax liability compared to the first updated return, this being a specific carve-out permitting a second filing

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) No; an updated return cannot be updated again - once an updated return has already been furnished for a tax year, the updated-return provisions cease to apply for that tax year

Section 263(6) expressly provides that the updated-return provisions do not apply where an updated return has already been furnished for that tax year - meaning an updated return cannot itself be 'updated' again for the same tax year.

question_html: If a person furnishes an updated return for a tax year, and as a result the loss (or unabsorbed depreciation, or tax credit) carried forward is required to be reduced for a subsequent tax year, what does section 263(6) require?

options.A: No further action is required; the reduction automatically and retrospectively adjusts the figures for all subsequent tax years without any further filing by the assessee
options.B: An updated return is required to be furnished for EACH such subsequent tax year in which the carried-forward loss, unabsorbed depreciation, or tax credit is to be correspondingly reduced
options.C: The assessee must instead file a fresh original return (not an updated return) for each such subsequent tax year, since updated returns are inapplicable to purely consequential adjustments
options.D: The assessee is required to notify the Assessing Officer in writing within 7 days, but is not required to furnish any further updated return for the subsequent tax years

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) An updated return is required to be furnished for EACH such subsequent tax year in which the carried-forward loss, unabsorbed depreciation, or tax credit is to be correspondingly reduced

Where furnishing an updated return for one tax year has the knock-on effect of reducing a loss, unabsorbed depreciation, or tax credit carried forward under Chapter VII/section 33(11)(b)/section 206(2)(e)-(h) for a subsequent tax year, section 263(6) requires the assessee to correspondingly furnish an updated return for each such subsequent tax year as well.

question_html: Before furnishing an updated return under section 263(6), what must the assessee do under section 267?

options.A: Simply file the updated return; no payment of any kind is required before furnishing an updated return, with any resulting tax liability being payable only after the return is processed
options.B: Pay only the additional income-tax computed under section 267(5), without any requirement to separately pay the underlying tax, interest, or fee before furnishing the updated return

question_html: Under section 267(5), what is the additional income-tax payable if the updated return is furnished after the expiry of the time available under section 263(4)/263(5), but before completion of 12 months from the end of the financial year succeeding the relevant tax year?

question_html: For the purpose of computing 'additional income-tax' under section 267(5), which of the following is correct?

options.A: 'Tax' would exclude surcharge and cess in every case, and the 'interest payable' would never be reduced by any interest paid in an earlier return, regardless of whether an earlier return was furnished
options.B: 'Tax' would include surcharge and cess (by whatever name called) on such tax, and the 'interest payable' would be the interest chargeable under any provision of the Act on the income as per the updated return, as reduced by any interest paid in the earlier return (this reduction being nil where no earlier return has been furnished)
options.C: 'Tax' and 'interest payable' are both computed strictly on the basis of the ORIGINAL return's figures, with no reference at all to the updated return's own income figures
options.D: The additional income-tax is computed as a flat percentage of the assessee's gross total income, without any reference to the tax or interest payable on the updated return

Correct answer: (B) 'Tax' would include surcharge and cess (by whatever name called) on such tax, and the 'interest payable' would be the interest chargeable under any provision of the Act on the income as per the updated return, as reduced by any interest paid in the earlier return (this reduction being nil where no earlier return has been furnished)

For computing additional income-tax under section 267(5): 'tax' includes surcharge and cess by whatever name called, and 'interest payable' means interest chargeable under any provision of the Act on the updated-return income, reduced by interest already paid in the earlier return (which reduction is nil if no earlier return was furnished at all).

question_html: Where the Assessing Officer considers a return of income furnished by the assessee to be defective, what is he required to do?

options.A: He must immediately treat the return as wholly invalid and proceed to complete a best-judgment assessment, without affording the assessee any opportunity to rectify the defect
options.B: He must refer the matter to the Principal Commissioner of Income-tax for a final determination, without directly communicating with the assessee regarding the defect
options.C: He may intimate the defect to the assessee and give him an opportunity to rectify the defect within 15 days from the date of such intimation (which period the Assessing Officer may extend, on an application by the assessee, beyond 15 days)

Under section 263(7), where the Assessing Officer considers a return defective, he may intimate the defect to the assessee and give him an opportunity to rectify it within 15 days of such intimation - a period the Assessing Officer may extend further on the assessee's application.

question_html: If the defect in a return is NOT rectified within the 15-day period (or such further extended period as the Assessing Officer may allow), what is the consequence?

options.A: The return continues to be treated as valid in all respects, with the defect being disregarded entirely once the 15-day period has lapsed without rectification

If the defect is not rectified within 15 days (or the extended period allowed), the return is treated as an invalid return, with the same consequences as if the assessee had failed to furnish any return of income at all.

question_html: Mrs. Hetal, an individual engaged in a beauty parlour business, has had her books of account audited under section 63 for the relevant tax year, with total income of Rs. 15,35,000. Can she furnish her return of income through a Tax Return Preparer under section 264?

options.A: Yes; every individual, regardless of any audit requirement, is entitled to furnish a return of income through a Tax Return Preparer under section 264, without exception

options.C: No, but only because she is a woman; the Tax Return Preparer scheme under section 264 is available exclusively to male assessees under the current statutory framework

The Tax Return Preparer scheme under section 264 does not extend to a person whose books of account are required to be audited under section 63. Since Mrs. Hetal's accounts have been audited under section 63, she cannot furnish her return of income through a Tax Return Preparer.

question_html: Under section 265, in what circumstance is an individual's return of income verified by someone OTHER than the individual himself?

options.A: Where the individual is mentally incapacitated from attending to his affairs (verified by his guardian or another competent person acting on his behalf), or where, for any other reason, it is not possible for the individual to verify the return (verified by a person duly authorised by him holding a valid power of attorney)
options.B: In every case, an individual's return must always be verified by a chartered accountant on his behalf, and the individual himself is never permitted to verify his own return
options.C: Only where the individual is outside India at the time of verification, this being the sole circumstance in which someone other than the individual may verify his return
options.D: Only where the individual's total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, this income threshold being the determinative factor for who may verify the return

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Where the individual is mentally incapacitated from attending to his affairs (verified by his guardian or another competent person acting on his behalf), or where, for any other reason, it is not possible for the individual to verify the return (verified by a person duly authorised by him holding a valid power of attorney)

Ordinarily, an individual verifies his own return. Exceptions arise where the individual is mentally incapacitated (verified by a guardian or other competent person acting on his behalf), or where it is otherwise not possible for him to verify the return (verified by a person holding a valid power of attorney from him).

question_html: Under section 265, an HUF's return of income is ordinarily verified by the Karta. In what circumstance is it instead verified by any OTHER adult member of the HUF?

An HUF's return is ordinarily verified by the Karta. Where the Karta is absent from India, or is mentally incapacitated from attending to his affairs, the return may instead be verified by any OTHER adult member of the HUF (who, per the Study Material, may be male or female).

question_html: Under section 265, the return of income of a company (other than the specific categories separately addressed, such as non-resident companies, companies being wound up, etc.) is ordinarily verified by whom?

question_html: Under section 265, the return of income of a firm is ordinarily verified by the managing partner, and the return of an LLP is ordinarily verified by the designated partner. In each case, if that person is unable to verify due to an unavoidable reason, or there is no such person, who may verify instead?

options.A: In both cases, only the Adjudicating Authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 may verify the return, regardless of the firm's or LLP's actual operational status
options.B: In both cases, verification must instead be undertaken personally by every single partner of the firm or LLP jointly, with no provision for verification by any one partner alone
options.C: In both cases, the return is treated as permanently unverifiable and invalid until a new managing partner or designated partner is formally appointed
options.D: In the case of a firm, any partner of the firm (not being a minor); in the case of an LLP, any partner of the LLP or any other person as may be prescribed for this purpose

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) In the case of a firm, any partner of the firm (not being a minor); in the case of an LLP, any partner of the LLP or any other person as may be prescribed for this purpose

Where the managing partner of a firm (or the designated partner of an LLP) is unable to verify the return due to an unavoidable reason, or there is no such person, a firm's return may be verified by any partner (not being a minor), and an LLP's return may be verified by any partner or such other person as may be prescribed.

question_html: Under section 266(1), where any tax is payable on the basis of a return required to be furnished under section 263, what must the assessee do before furnishing that return?

question_html: Where the amount paid by the assessee under section 266(1) falls short of the aggregate of tax, interest, and fee due, in what ORDER is the amount so paid adjusted?

options.A: First towards the tax payable, thereafter towards the interest payable, and the balance (if any) towards the fee payable
options.B: First towards the fee payable, thereafter towards the interest payable, and the balance (if any) towards the tax payable

Section 266(3) prescribes a specific priority order for adjusting a shortfall: FIRST towards fee, THEN towards interest, and only the remaining balance (if any) towards tax - fee and interest are settled ahead of the principal tax liability.

question_html: What is the consequence under section 266(8)/(9) if an assessee fails to pay the whole or any part of the tax, interest, or fee referred to in section 266?

options.A: No specific consequence arises under section 266 itself; the assessee's only exposure is the ordinary interest that would in any event accrue under section 423 for delay in payment
options.B: The return of income is automatically and permanently treated as withdrawn, as though it had never been furnished at all, regardless of the amount of the shortfall

Under section 266(8)/(9), failure to pay the whole or part of the tax/interest/fee renders the assessee 'an assessee in default' in respect of the unpaid amount, attracting the ordinary consequences the Act provides for such default - and this is expressly stated not to limit any OTHER consequences the assessee may separately incur.

question_html: Under section 262(1), a person whose total income (or the total income of any other person for which he is assessable) exceeds the maximum amount not chargeable to tax during a tax year is required to apply for PAN by when?

question_html: Under section 262, is a person who has NOT been allotted a PAN but possesses an Aadhaar Number permitted to quote the Aadhaar Number in lieu of PAN?

options.A: Yes; a person who has not been allotted a PAN but possesses the Aadhaar Number may intimate/quote/furnish his Aadhaar Number in lieu of PAN, and a PAN would then be allotted to him in the prescribed manner
options.B: No; every person is mandatorily required to first obtain a PAN before quoting either PAN or Aadhaar Number in any document, correspondence, or challan under the Act

Correct answer: (A) Yes; a person who has not been allotted a PAN but possesses the Aadhaar Number may intimate/quote/furnish his Aadhaar Number in lieu of PAN, and a PAN would then be allotted to him in the prescribed manner

Section 262 permits interchangeability: a person who has not been allotted a PAN but possesses an Aadhaar Number may intimate/quote/furnish the Aadhaar Number in lieu of PAN (with PAN then allotted to him in the prescribed manner); conversely, a person allotted PAN who has intimated his Aadhaar Number to the prescribed authority may also quote Aadhaar in lieu of PAN.

question_html: Under section 467(1), what penalty may the Assessing Officer impose on a person for failure to comply with the provisions of section 262?

Section 263(1) compulsorily requires a resident other than not ordinarily resident (ROR) who has signing authority in any account located outside India, at any time during the tax year, to furnish a return - and this obligation exists irrespective of whether income earned/loss incurred during the tax year, and therefore irrespective of the basic exemption limit.

'Beneficial owner' means a person who has provided, directly or indirectly, consideration for the asset for the immediate or future benefit, direct or indirect, of himself OR any other person. question_html: Can Mr. Karthik carry forward the short-term capital loss of Rs. 1,20,000, given that he has not furnished any return (original or belated) for the tax year?

options.A: No; section 121 mandates timely filing of a return of loss on or before the due date under section 263(1)(c) for carry forward of capital loss under section 111(1), and since Mr. Karthik has not furnished any return at all, he cannot carry forward this capital loss
options.B: Yes; capital loss can always be carried forward irrespective of whether any return has been furnished, exactly like house property loss and unabsorbed depreciation
options.C: Yes, but only up to 50% of the loss amount, this being a specific statutory limitation applicable where the return has not been furnished within the due date
options.D: No, but only because he has exercised the option of shifting out of the default tax regime; had he remained under the default regime, the capital loss could have been carried forward without any return being furnished

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) No; section 121 mandates timely filing of a return of loss on or before the due date under section 263(1)(c) for carry forward of capital loss under section 111(1), and since Mr. Karthik has not furnished any return at all, he cannot carry forward this capital loss

Capital loss under section 111(1) is one of the losses requiring timely filing (on or before the section 263(1)(c) due date) under section 121, for it to be eligible for carry forward. Since Mr. Karthik filed no return at all, he forfeits the ability to carry forward the Rs. 1,20,000 short-term capital loss.

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) By any other adult member of the HUF

Section 265 provides that where the Karta of an HUF is absent from India, or is mentally incapacitated from attending to his affairs, the return of income may be verified by any OTHER adult member of the HUF - such member may be male or female, and this is precisely Mr. Chandran's situation here.
